newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Some member states want agrimoney change before 1999.
newsitem.headline: Some member states want agrimoney change before 1999.

text.p: Several member states, including France, are against plans to leave the EU's agrimonetary rules generally unchanged ahead of the introduction of a single currency in 1999, EU officials said on Thursday.
In a report last month, the European Commission only suggested some simplification and tidying up of the system, notably the abolition of green rates for agricultural imports.
The conversion rate for agricultural imports would in future be based on a single rate -- the twice monthly common customs tariff market rate -- and make life easier for traders, officials said.
"Keeping green rates for agricultural imports would be incompatible with WTO (World Trade Organisation) rules," said one official.
The EU's agrimonetary committee is discussing the issue further.
